summary: This PR archives the S-17 Bread calibration experiment, adding measurement harness scripts and experiment records without touching production engine, API, or database behavior. The reviewer found no critical or security issues; instead, a handful of minor correctness bugs in auxiliary tooling (contact-sheet aspect distortion, compare-mode crash paths violating the tool's own exit-code contract) and small style/duplication nits (shared constants duplicated between two stats scripts, one dead code branch). The most notable risk is F3: the bilinear sampler reproducing Chromium's drawImage behavior — explicitly called out as having previously flipped an experiment result — lacks a golden-pixel regression test despite being the most fragile, consequential logic in the diff. Given the non-production scope, passing validation gates per the PR metadata, and the minor severity of all findings, the change is acceptable to merge as archival/tooling work, though the identified gaps should be tracked for follow-up.

findings.description: `STAT_FIELDS`/`FIELDS`, the `PERCENTILES` set, and the tolerance/bin-rounding logic are duplicated between `browser-stats.ts` and `desktop-stats.ts`; the two will drift when the LumaStats shape or a threshold changes.
findings.suggestion: Move the field list and percentile set into `scripts/s17/harness.ts` next to the existing shared record shapes.

findings.description: `original.resize(target, ...)` forces the original into the exact pixel box of the smallest Bread output. The `note` on line 143 only fires when outputs differ from each other; if a single output's aspect ratio differs from the source's, the original is silently distorted on the sheet the maintainer tunes from — the artifact where aspect distortion is most misleading.
findings.suggestion: Compare the original's aspect ratio to `target`; on mismatch either letterbox or print a warning alongside the existing size note.

findings.description: `point_bilinear` (and the jpeg-draft pipeline around it) hand-reproduces Chromium's `drawImage` sampler, including floor-half-up rounding. The docstring itself records that small sampler differences flipped S17-04 across the 0.005 clip guard (Cloud gamma 1.50 vs 1.10). This is exactly the kind of fragile numeric behavior that deserves a golden test, yet the diff adds none — a future cleanup of the rounding or a Pillow drift would go unnoticed.
findings.suggestion: Add a small golden-pixel test: a stored small source image plus expected sampled output array (captured from a verified run), asserted against `point_bilinear` and the jpeg-draft path.

findings.description: `compare()` verifies each baseline id exists in the download, but not the reverse: if the baseline lacks an id, `a` is `undefined` and `auto(a)` throws a TypeError instead of exiting 1 with a message naming the id — violating the tool's own exit-status contract (1 = comparison could not run).
findings.suggestion: Check `if (!a) { console.error(`${id}: missing from ${baselinePath}`); process.exit(1); }` before calling `auto(a)`.

findings.description: `--compare` mode is dispatched at module scope (line 155), but lines 145–150 already read and hash every licensed tuning photo at load time and throw on mismatch or missing files. Since `test-photos/private/` is gitignored, `--compare <download.json>` on any machine without the inputs dies with an unhandled throw instead of the documented "exit 1, comparison could not run" behavior.
findings.suggestion: Move the photo loading loop after the `--compare` dispatch (or gate it behind a `serve` code path) so compare mode needs only the baseline and download files.

findings.description: `run.imageLabel.startsWith("data:")` is dead code: `imageLabel` is always the local path or a remote URL, never a data URI, so the ternary's first branch can never be taken.
findings.suggestion: Drop the ternary and record `run.imageLabel` directly (the local path is the more useful record anyway).

implementation_correctness.justification: Several concrete correctness bugs were found in the tooling (F2 contact-sheet aspect distortion, F4 missing-id crash instead of documented exit 1, F5 --compare mode dying on load-time file reads before dispatch), but all are confined to auxiliary experiment scripts that the PR explicitly states do not touch production engine/API/DB behavior, limiting blast radius.

idiomaticity.justification: Minor style issues only: dead/unreachable branch in bread-spike.ts (F6) and duplicated constants/logic across two stats scripts (F1) that should be centralized in the existing shared harness module. Neither suggests the code fights language/project conventions broadly.

complexity.justification: The duplication flagged in F1 (field lists, percentile sets, tolerance logic repeated between browser-stats.ts and desktop-stats.ts) adds avoidable accidental complexity and drift risk, but no finding suggests the overall design is over-engineered or hard to follow.

test_risk_coverage.justification: F3 identifies that the most fragile, outcome-determining logic in the PR — the bilinear sampler reproducing Chromium's drawImage rounding, which the docstring itself says flipped a key experiment result — ships with no golden/regression test, leaving the riskiest numeric path uncovered despite the large test suite passing overall.

documentation.justification: No findings call out missing or misleading documentation; the PR body indicates substantial archival documentation (plan, decision record, roadmap/issue updates). The one note-related gap (F2) is a correctness/behavior issue rather than a documentation gap, so it is not scored here.

security_safety.justification: No findings identify any security, secret-handling, or untrusted-input vulnerability; private tuning photos are gitignored and the changes are confined to internal experiment tooling.

verdictReason: All findings are minor or nit-level issues confined to auxiliary experiment/archival tooling with no production impact, and the PR's stated validation (typecheck, 418 tests, lint, parity checks) passed; the one notable gap is missing test coverage for a fragile numeric sampler (F3), which should be addressed but does not by itself warrant failing the change.
